Spinner · Relay × Mesh

Your combination: a force graph that is still settling, with a signal relaying around its edges. The graph is the substrate, the relay is what is happening on it.

Combining them makes one new decision — how much the substrate moves. Too little and it is Relay with a wobble; too much and the relay is lost inside it. So the three below differ in exactly that and in nothing else: same nodes, same relay, same timing. The settle runs at twice the relay period, so the two never drift into a beat against each other.

J · Calm substrate — relay leads

The graph drifts: 20° of rotation and a tenth of its size. The relay is unmistakably the rhythm and the settling is something you notice second, which is what keeps it readable at 14px.

What to look for in the 14px column. At that size a node is about 3px and an edge is one. The question is not whether it is pretty — it is whether you can still tell that a signal is going round, or whether it has become a shape that shimmers.
